# docker_secret (Resource)

A Swarm secret: an immutable blob the Swarm managers store encrypted and mount into service tasks under `/run/secrets/<file_name>`. Requires the provider to point at a Swarm manager. Swarm secrets cannot be changed after creation, so every change replaces the secret; a secret still referenced by a service cannot be removed, so change the referencing service in the same apply (or use `create_before_destroy` with a new name).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_secret" "db_password" {
  name = "db_password"
  data = base64encode("change-me")

  labels = {
    app = "shop"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `data` (String, Sensitive) Secret content, base64-encoded (use `base64encode()`); it must decode. The daemon never returns secret data, so it is kept from state on refresh and ignored on import. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `name` (String) Secret name, unique in the Swarm. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `labels` (Map of String) User labels on the secret. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The Swarm secret ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by secret name or ID. The daemon never returns secret data, so
# the next plan replaces the secret unless data is ignored or recreated.
terraform import docker_secret.db_password db_password
```
